findings.condition: DIER/ARR restoration entered and either LPTIM_WaitFlag returns HAL_ERROR.
findings.observation: Lines939/945 return with PRIMASK still1; saved mask restored only on success at959. Saved PRIMASK=0 is the state-loss case; an entry value1 remains masked.
findings.scope: Pinned SDK source finding; no hardware timeout reproduced.

findings.condition: Default interrupt-driven HAL tick, PRIMASK=1, required hardware flag never asserts.
findings.observation: HAL_GetTick reads uwTick; default increments in SysTick ISR. Timeout cannot be assumed to advance with interrupts masked.
findings.scope: Potential unbounded wait under stated conditions; alternate tick requires separate audit. With the default stopped tick and a never-set flag, the error exits in finding1 are not reached; an advancing override may instead reach them.

findings.observation: All three callers set IDLE despite helper error, then return error. IDLE does not establish hardware release.

findings.condition: HAL_LPTIM_SetConfigEncoder accepts IDLE|ACTIVE by debug assertion and calls LL_LPTIM_Disable.
findings.observation: Path does not use RCC-reset helper. ES2.6.1 compliance/quiescence must be established before active configuration. LL clears CR.ENABLE; occurrence requires relevant interrupt timing and subsequent Stop entry.
findings.scope: No hardware failure reproduced; timing conditions remain material.

findings.condition: Application relies on a single HAL_RTC_CALENDAR_GetDateTime call as the complete ES2.7.2 workaround.
findings.observation: Wrapper reads time and date once; inspected helpers do not perform two consecutive full-calendar reads and compare. An adapter must explicitly establish BYPSHAD=1 and the repeat-until-matching protocol, with its own deadline/failure policy.
findings.scope: Caller may already wrap this API; no claim that all applications fail or hardware fault was reproduced.

findings.condition: Spurious controller-mode BERR with ERRIE enabled reaches stock HAL_I2C_ERR_IRQHandler.
findings.observation: Handler clears BERR and calls I2C_ITError; that path resets transfer fields and interrupts and can set IDLE. This is more than the ES2.8.2 clear-and-continue protocol. Adapter policy must distinguish this controller-mode case from genuine/other errors.
findings.scope: No hardware event reproduced; external wrappers or alternate handlers may already handle the condition. Polling/blocking I2C path remains unaudited in this artifact.

findings.condition: User selects analog LSE bypass or low-drive crystal operation on an ES0676 listed revision.
findings.observation: HAL_RCC_LSE_Enable accepts those enum/drive domains and programs the registers without the ES2.2.1/2.2.3 exclusions. Admission must apply digital-only bypass and forbid low crystal drive explicitly.
findings.scope: Raw register/SDK expressibility does not imply errata-qualified operation; no hardware failure reproduced. ES names RCC_BDCR while exact SDK uses RCC_RTCCR; preserve the spelling difference.

Buffer may have been partially written before failure; status is required before interpreting the requested block as complete.
Recovery checks final SECS and returnsHAL_ERROR if stillset; configuration may be adapted.

observations: RM message-RAM allocation has three Tx elements, 18 words each; HAL exposes TX_BUFFER_0,1,2; TXBAR add-request field has bits 2:0 only.
ES example dedicated buffers 4/5 is outside this exact reviewed slot domain and cannot be used as an executable recipe.
Source hardware allocation is 212 32-bit words per instance, 0x350 bytes; FIFO mode and queue mode use TFQM.
RM2044 uses slot indices 0..2, while p2077 FIFO index prose says0..3; keep this discrepancy explicit rather than allocating a fourth slot.

TXBC exposes only TFQM for the three elements as FIFO or queue; ES assumes dedicated buffer plus FIFO, requiring reconciliation. Queue TFQM=1 lies outside the literal ES condition; no general immunity inferred.
Other ES candidates fit the slot inventory: only one FIFO element pending at a time, or FIFO only. This does not establish full workaround qualification.
RM2077 index wording corresponds to two-bit TFQPI/TFGI fields; reset TXFQS=0x00000003 means free level3, consistent with three slots.
remaining: ES mixed dedicated-buffer/FIFO applicability requires exact IP interpretation
Preserve RM2021 one-module prose versus exact two-instance inventory conflict
Clock/pin/bit-timing/message-RAM ownership and runtime lifecycle
No general immunity to ES2.12.2 inferred from unavailable example buffers

observations: LL sampling setter documents disabled or enabled-without-regular-conversion state and only modifies CFGR2. It does not perform the ES disable/clear/re-enable sequence.

HAL SetConfig checks INIT/CONFIGURING/IDLE via debug assertion and calls the setter directly. A valid successful stop can disable the ADC; this is not evidence that ordinary legal HAL transitions necessarily violate the erratum.

HAL Stop calls adc_deactivate, then sets global IDLE even if returned status is HAL_ERROR. The helper can reject ongoing conversion or time out while ADEN remains set. IDLE alone therefore cannot establish physical disable before changing SMPTRIG.
If ADDIS is already set on entry, adc_deactivate can skip its outer body and return HAL_OK without waiting. Successful status alone is insufficient outside the controlled ordinary path.
remaining: Track relevant SMPTRIG and conversion history; enforce disabled state and full ES sequence before injected conversion.
Require successful stop status plus hardware quiescence under ownership; audit regular/injected stop paths and every caller.
Tick progress and timeout policy remain prerequisites; no observed ADC failure claimed.

observations: HAL EnableReadyPin checks IDLE by debug assertion and returns HAL_ERROR when IO lock is set; otherwise sets RDIOM. This function does not validate data width or external serial-clock/APB ratio.
RM1960 independently prohibits RDY for frames shorter than 8 bits. This closes the <8-bit admission gap left unlisted in the erratum, without inventing an erratum threshold for them.

For slave RDY, ES thresholds are serial clock greater than 2x APB for 8..15 bits, 6x for 16..23,14x for 24..32. Satisfying these frequency bounds alone does not qualify an electrical or runtime configuration.
remaining: Exact instance/package RDY pin routing, external-master compliance and measured serial/APB clocks.
FIFO service, TSIZE end-of-transfer semantics, and all ordinary SPI electrical/timing limits remain separate.
24..32-bit failure thresholds matter only on instances supporting those frame widths; these are failure conditions, not sufficient admission criteria.

observations: ES qualifies nominal RM ONEBIT suppression: noise on START can still set NE. No workaround; received-data validity is not established.
SetOneBitSample programs the mode; state and LPUART-exclusion guards are debug assertions.

IRQ path records and clears NE when EIE is enabled without excluding ONEBIT. Under normal error dispatch, DMA reception takes the blocking path, ends reception and can abort DMA; non-DMA NE-only handling can notify and continue.

RM DDRE=0 describes no DMA request for an erroneous byte while later correct bytes may transfer. This hardware behavior does not negate EIE-driven HAL error/abort handling; silent continuation is not guaranteed.

RM DDRE=1 requires DMAR disabled or RXNE/RXFNE cleared before clearing error flags. Inspected HAL clears NE before later abort handling; exact DDRE setup/order and receive-path behavior require further audit, not a claim of observed corruption.
remaining: ONEBIT must not imply NE impossible or uninterrupted DMA reception.
Do not suppress NE as harmless; preserve simultaneous ORE/RTO/other errors, callback synchronization and buffer ownership.
Bind exact ONEBIT-capable instances and DDRE configuration before executable admission.
